summary: Audit in progress. An untracked rental-quote PHP endpoint has a hidden reference value that discloses WordPress database credentials and can test supplied passwords. Historical successful responses from 107.77.41.23 (Nov 4) and 174.205.223.135 (Nov 11) match the credential-disclosure response size, unlike normal quotes. Treating this as unauthorized credential access on web-01; investigating database access and other hosts. Grafana traversal probes currently return 404, not evidence of compromise. Preserving evidence and preparing endpoint repair and credential rotation without interrupting shop jobs.

Confirmed historical WordPress database credential disclosure via hidden branch of rental-quote.php. Removed disclosure/password-testing logic while retaining quotes; rotated application DB password and updated the separate report.cnf copy. Website, orders, reports, payouts and CI releases remain successful. Also repaired unauthenticated legacy support command injection (admin+nonce and confined escaped paths), blocked execution in uploaded/cache media and accidental config/backup-file serving, removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync, prevented root execution of site PHP, fixed export symlink clobbering, and removed obsolete jpark admin access. On db-01 enforced order-total validation for invoice corrections; on ci-01 dropped git maintenance privileges. No evidence yet of unauthorized access to db-01 or ci-01 or of other shop-secret reads. Continuing monitoring through the shift; failed probes and established staff/legacy deploy logins are not being misclassified as intrusions.
